Prerequisites: 03 · Triangles, area and surface normals

An address inside a triangle

Barycentric coordinates describe a point as a weighted mixture of a triangle's corners. The weights sum to one. Inside a nondegenerate triangle they are nonnegative; on an edge one is zero; outside, at least one can be negative. They are coordinates relative to this triangle, not a universal location that can be transferred to an unrelated mesh.

The same weights can interpolate colors, texture coordinates or other per-corner attributes. A shared geometric vertex may have different texture coordinates on either side of a seam, which is why per-face-corner attributes are useful. Interpolated normals generally need normalization afterward; averaging unit vectors does not preserve unit length.

Worked example

For a=(0,0), b=(2,0), c=(0,3) and weights (0.2,0.3,0.5), the point is (0.6,1.5). Give the corners values (10,20,40) and the interpolated value is 28. This is not nearest-corner lookup: all three corners contribute. The result stays between the minimum and maximum values when weights are nonnegative and sum to one.

Perspective changes the weights

Weights measured after perspective projection are screen-space weights. They generally cannot interpolate a world-space attribute directly. Divide each screen weight by the corner's clip weight w, then renormalize. The denominator must be valid; clipping and singularities remain separate concerns.

At a screen midpoint between corners with w values one and two, equal screen weights become two thirds and one third. An attribute zero at the first corner and one at the second therefore evaluates to one third, not one half.

Try it yourself

What happens if all three clip weights are equal?

Answer

The common factor cancels. Perspective-correct and screen-space weights agree.

gffx boundary

The existing interpolate primitive applies supplied weights; it does not infer their intended coordinate system. The rasterizer supplies screen-space barycentrics. Callers needing perspective correction must construct the correct weights explicitly. Discrete face IDs and background selection do not gain derivatives just because attribute interpolation is differentiable. Test the gather, weights and interpolation together to catch corner-order mistakes.
